scenario: Frustrated user trying to open Mooziac on macOS Sequoia and receiving the Gatekeeper damaged alert.

messages.content: yo i just downloaded mooziac and macos says it's damaged and tells me to move it to trash?? wtf is this malware

No worries, it's definitely not malware! That error is macOS Gatekeeper's generic message whenever an open-source app isn't signed with an expensive Apple Developer ID certificate.

You can fix this in about 5 seconds:
1. Open Terminal on your Mac.
2. Paste this command and hit Enter:
   xattr -cr /Applications/Mooziac.app

That clears Apple's quarantine flag and Mooziac will open right up!
ok that worked immediately lol thanks. why doesnt apple just say that instead of damaged

Apple defaults to the 'damaged' warning for unnotarized apps downloaded from browsers on recent macOS versions like Ventura, Sonoma, and Sequoia. Once you strip the quarantine extended attribute, macOS treats it normally. Glad you're up and running!

scenario: User cannot get edge volume to respond and thinks the feature is broken.

messages.content: why tf is the volume gesture not working?? i'm sliding on my trackpad and literally nothing happens

Let's get that working for you! Mooziac's Edge Volume gesture has two specific spatial requirements to make sure it doesn't trigger accidentally while you're typing:

1. Starting Zone: You must place your finger in the top 30% of your trackpad, right along the far right edge (within ~2.5mm of the outer rim).
2. Movement: You need to slide up or down by at least 3mm before the volume slider kicks in.

Could you try placing your finger at the top-right edge and sliding downwards in one smooth motion?
ohhhh wait i was starting from the middle of the trackpad. doing it from the top right works!! does it work with a normal mouse too or only trackpad?

Awesome! The Edge Volume gesture relies on Apple's private MultitouchSupport framework, which reads raw digitizer touch coordinates from built-in MacBook trackpads and Apple Magic Trackpads. Standard USB or Bluetooth mice don't send those multitouch events.

However, if you're using a mouse, you can scroll directly over Mooziac's menu bar icon at the top of your screen to adjust volume effortlessly!

scenario: User downloaded songs from YouTube Music but cannot locate the files on their Mac.

messages.content: bro where did my music go? it said download complete but i can't find it anywhere in my downloads folder

Mooziac doesn't save music into your general 'Downloads' folder. By default, it stores all downloaded tracks in your user Music directory:
~/Music/Mooziac/

To view them in Finder:
1. Open Finder.
2. Press Cmd+Shift+G (Go to Folder).
3. Enter: ~/Music/Mooziac

Your songs should all be there tagged with title, artist, and artwork!
found them! can i change that folder to an external hard drive?

Yes! Open Mooziac Settings (Cmd+,), go to the Downloads tab, and click 'Change Download Location'. You can select any folder on your Mac or a connected external hard drive. All future downloads will go straight there.

scenario: User playing a local track or lesser-known song and lyrics are missing.

messages.content: yo why aren't my lyrics showing? it just says 'No lyrics available' for half my songs

Mooziac checks several sources for synced lyrics: local `.lrc` files, YouTube Music, and LRCLib's community database. If a song is an indie track, rare remix, or local rip, an automated match might not exist yet.

Are the songs without lyrics local files or streamed through YouTube Music?
they're local flac files i imported from my drive

For local files, the best and most reliable solution is to place a `.lrc` file right next to your audio file with the exact same name.

For example:
- `Daft Punk - Veridis Quo.flac`
- `Daft Punk - Veridis Quo.lrc`

Mooziac's SyncedLyricsParser will immediately load the `.lrc` file and scroll the lyrics in real time under the notch without needing any internet connection!

scenario: User listening to music but their Discord status does not show Mooziac.

messages.content: why is discord not showing what I'm listening to? i have discord open

Let's check three quick settings:

1. Inside Mooziac: Open Settings (Cmd+,) > Integrations, and make sure 'Discord Rich Presence' is toggled ON.
2. Inside Discord: Open Discord User Settings (gear icon) > Activity Privacy, and verify that 'Display current activity as a status message' is turned ON.
3. Discord App: Make sure you're using the native Discord desktop app on macOS. Discord running in a web browser (like Chrome or Safari) cannot receive local Unix domain socket IPC connections.
ah i had 'display current activity' off in discord. turned it on and it immediately popped up with the album cover and track time! that's so clean
Awesome! Mooziac talks directly to the local Discord socket (/tmp/discord-ipc-0) without needing any Node.js background daemons, so it updates instantly with zero battery drain.

im on 1.1.6

That explains it! Go to Mooziac > Check for Updates… and update to v1.1.7 (or download the latest DMG from GitHub). In v1.1.7+, trackpad scrolling over the menu bar item increments volume in 2% steps smoothly while filtering out inertia momentum.

scenario: User asking why they should switch from Spotify to Mooziac and whether it handles lossless music.

messages.content: why would I use this over spotify or web player? what's the big deal

Here are the main advantages of Mooziac:

1. Native macOS Performance: Spotify is an Electron app taking 500MB+ of RAM. Mooziac is pure Swift/AppKit, taking only 40-90MB RAM with ~1% CPU.
2. Lossless Local Audio: Spotify can't play 24-bit/192kHz FLAC or WAV properly. Mooziac supports FLAC, MP3, WAV, OPUS, and AIFF with bit-perfect rendering.
3. Native macOS Gestures: Adjust volume directly from your trackpad's right edge or scroll on the menu bar without switching windows.
4. Centered Notch Lyrics HUD: Real-time synced lyrics docked right under your MacBook camera notch.
5. Complete Privacy: Zero trackers, zero telemetry, and your data stays on your Mac.
does it support flac files? can i use my own music and stream at the same time?

Yes! You can load your local FLAC library into Mooziac (Cmd+O to add your music folder) and also browse/stream YouTube Music in the streaming tab. Both seamlessly share the same queue, player controls, lyrics engine, and trackpad gestures.

scenario: User confused why music stopped when pulling out headphones.

messages.content: my song just stopped playing out of nowhere when i took my airpods out, is that a bug?

That is actually an intentional safety feature! Mooziac includes an AudioRouteMonitor that listens for macOS CoreAudio device changes (kAudioHardwarePropertyDefaultOutputDevice).

When your AirPods or wired headphones disconnect, Mooziac automatically pauses playback so your music doesn't suddenly blast through your Mac's built-in speakers in a quiet room or library. You can simply hit Spacebar to resume whenever you're ready.
oh thats actually really smart. nice touch!
Thanks! It's one of those native macOS touches designed to make the experience smooth and respectful of your environment.

scenario: User complaining that a rock album sounds much quieter than on Spotify or Apple Music.

messages.content: how do I make this louder? why are some songs so quiet even when my volume is turned up?

This is likely caused by Loudness Normalization. Mooziac includes an automatic volume normalizer calibrated to -14 LUFS (the standard streaming target).

Modern hyper-compressed tracks are attenuated to match softer classical or acoustic recordings so you don't get volume spikes. If you prefer raw, uncompressed volume:
1. Open Mooziac Settings (Cmd+,).
2. Go to the Audio tab.
3. Uncheck 'Loudness Normalization'.

Also make sure Mooziac's internal App Volume slider is pushed all the way to 100%!
unchecking that brought back the punch, thanks! what does LUFS mean anyway?

LUFS stands for 'Loudness Units relative to Full Scale'. It measures human perceived loudness over time rather than just electrical peak voltage. -14 LUFS is the standard level used by YouTube Music, Spotify, and European broadcast standards to prevent 'loudness wars'.

scenario: User experiencing spacebar pausing music while searching for songs on YouTube Music.

messages.content: why does hitting spacebar inside the search bar pause my music instead of typing a space?! so annoying

This was an issue in early versions where the global hotkey handler intercepted the spacebar before the web text input received it. We resolved this in update v1.1.7: Mooziac now checks whether a web input element has first-responder focus before toggling playback.

Updating to v1.1.7 or later will permanently fix this! In the meantime, you can either click outside the input box to play/pause, or paste your search query with spaces.
just updated to 1.1.7 and the search bar works normally now with spaces. thank you!
Glad to hear! Keep enjoying Mooziac, and feel free to reach out if you hit anything else.

scenario: User accidentally skipping songs while resting wrists on MacBook trackpad.

messages.content: my songs keep randomly skipping while i'm typing an essay! is my trackpad haunted

Haha, not haunted! By default, Mooziac has trackpad corner gestures enabled. If your wrist or palm rests in the bottom-right corner (within 2.5mm of the corner) and taps twice, Mooziac interprets that as the 'Next Track' shortcut.

You have two options:
1. Open Settings > Gestures and toggle OFF 'Enable Corner Tap Triggers'.
2. Or keep it on, but remap the bottom-right corner to 'None' or 'Toggle Lyrics' so it doesn't interrupt your playback.
turned off corner taps and kept edge volume on. perfect! no more accidental skips
Great! That's why the settings are modular—you can keep the edge volume slide for quick volume adjustments while disabling corner taps if your typing posture triggers them.

scenario: User with external monitor asking about Centered Lyrics HUD positioning.

messages.content: can I put the lyrics under the mac notch? and what happens when i plug into my external 4k monitor?

Yes! The Centered Lyrics HUD is specifically sculpted to dock immediately beneath the MacBook display notch.

When you connect an external monitor, Mooziac detects the currently active display screen (the screen containing the focused window or mouse pointer) and automatically docks the HUD centered along the top menu bar of that monitor.
how do i show or hide it quickly?
You can toggle the HUD anytime by pressing Cmd+Shift+L, or by performing a quick 3-tap gesture in the bottom-left corner of your trackpad!

scenario: User on an older Intel MacBook Pro noticing fan spin with animated waveform.

messages.content: does this work on an intel mac? my fans are ramping up slightly when playing music

Yes, Mooziac is a Universal 2 binary with native x86_64 code for Intel Macs as well as arm64 for Apple Silicon.

If you're noticing fan spin on an older Intel Mac with integrated graphics, check your Progress Bar Style in Settings > Appearance. If it is set to 'Waveform', it animates 32 reactive bars continuously, which can trigger Intel GPU rendering.

Try switching the Progress Bar Style to 'Minimal Line' and your Theme to 'OLED Dark Mode'. That eliminates active animation loops and drops CPU usage below 1%.
switched to minimal line and fans went completely silent. thanks!
Awesome! Minimal Line uses simple single-path AppKit strokes with zero GPU shading, making it ideal for conserving battery and keeping older Intel Macs cool.

scenario: Audiophile asking for 10-band graphic equalizer and bass boost.

messages.content: does mooziac have an equalizer? how do i turn up the bass for my headphones

Currently, Mooziac does not have a built-in graphic equalizer or bass booster. Playback is rendered flat and bit-perfect as intended by the audio mastering, with optional -14 LUFS loudness normalization.

A 10-band graphic EQ is one of the most requested features on our GitHub. You can follow or upvote the request at https://github.com/shirkeharsh/mooziac/issues.

In the meantime, system-level audio tools like eqMac or SoundSource work seamlessly alongside Mooziac if you need custom EQ profiles.

scenario: User asking how to cleanly wipe all traces of Mooziac.

messages.content: how do I uninstall it? i want to make sure all cached files and databases are gone too

To perform a 100% clean uninstall of Mooziac:

1. Move Mooziac.app from your `/Applications` folder to the Trash.
2. Delete application support files:
   `rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Mooziac`
3. Delete cached lyrics and web data:
   `rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/Mooziac`
   `rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/site.threeten.mooziac`
4. Remove preferences:
   `rm -f ~/Library/Preferences/site.threeten.mooziac.plist`

Note: If you downloaded songs to `~/Music/Mooziac/`, they won't be deleted automatically unless you remove that folder as well.
super clear instructions. thanks!
You're welcome! Let us know if you ever decide to give Mooziac another try in the future.

scenario: Developer wanting to contribute and build the project locally.

messages.content: how do i build mooziac from source? i want to inspect the swift code

Building Mooziac from source is very straightforward because it has zero external CocoaPods or Carthage dependencies!

Here are the steps:
1. Clone the repo:
   git clone https://github.com/shirkeharsh/mooziac.git
   cd mooziac
2. Make sure you have Xcode 15+ installed (with Swift 5.9+ Command Line Tools).
3. Run the automated build script:
   ./build_app.sh

The script compiles both arm64 and x86_64 architectures into a Universal binary, sets entitlements and Info.plist, and outputs the finished app in `dist/Mooziac.app`.
ran build_app.sh and got dist/Mooziac.app with zero errors. thanks man
Awesome! Feel free to submit a pull request on GitHub if you build something cool.

scenario: User's download failed because yt-dlp was corrupted during a wifi drop.

messages.content: downloads fail immediately with helper binary error! my wifi cut out while it was setting up the first time

It sounds like the automated yt-dlp helper binary download was interrupted, leaving a partially downloaded or corrupt file in your application support folder.

Here is how to reset it:
1. Quit Mooziac.
2. Open Terminal and run:
   rm -f ~/Library/Application\ Support/Mooziac/bin/yt-dlp
3. Re-open Mooziac and try downloading the track again.

Mooziac's DependencyManager will detect that the binary is missing and cleanly re-download the latest official binary from GitHub.
that did it! it downloaded cleanly and now my songs are downloading at full speed
Excellent! DependencyManager verifies binary integrity upon every fresh download.

scenario: Privacy-conscious user asking if Mooziac transmits usage analytics or tracks listening history.

messages.content: does mooziac track my IP address, listening stats, or send analytics back to any servers?

Absolutely not. Mooziac has zero telemetry, zero analytics SDKs, and zero tracking code.

Here is how network traffic is handled:
- Listening History & Playlists: Stored 100% locally on your machine in SQLite (~/Library/Application Support/Mooziac/mooziac.sqlite).
- Streaming: If you use YouTube Music, requests go directly between your Mac and Google's servers via WebKit.
- Synced Lyrics: Fetched directly from LRCLib API or YouTube Music.
- Discord Rich Presence: Communicates locally via a Unix domain socket on your Mac—no internet connection involved.
- Update Checker: Checks public GitHub releases API.

Nothing about your identity, files, or music habits is ever transmitted to us or any third party.
that is so refreshing to hear in 2026. keep up the great work!
Thank you! Protecting user privacy and keeping software lightweight and native are our core principles.
